title: Multi-ancestry proteome-phenome-wide atlas through Mendelian randomization (Phenome-wide 2024)
bodyHtml:
Circulating proteins influence disease risk and are valuable drug targets, yet existing studies have mainly focused on European ancestry populations. To enhance the discovery of protein-phenotype associations and identify potential therapeutic targets across diverse populations, we conducted proteome-phenome-wide Mendelian randomization in three ancestries with seven cohorts, followed by comprehensive sensitivity analyses.

We tested the potential causal effect of up to 2,265 unique proteins on 355 phenotypes with 726,035 protein-phenotype pairs in European (173,748 in ARIC, 182,433 in deCODE, 180,018 in Fenland, and 189,836 in UKB-PPP), 33,078 in African ancestries (20,442 in ARIC and 12,636 in UKB-PPP), and 115,352 in East Asian ancestry populations.

In European ancestries, we identified a total of 6,771 putatively causal protein-phenotype associations (1,764 pairs in ARIC; 1,731 in deCODE, 1,788 in Fenland, and 1,488 in UKB-PPP) pertaining to 3,949 unique pairs. In African ancestries, we identified a total of 72 associations involving 35 associations in ARIC and 37 associations in UKB-PPP, with 56 unique protein-phenotype associations across both cohorts involving 28 proteins and 11 phenotypes. In East Asian ancestries, 339 putatively causal associations were identified with 325 unique protein-phenotype pairs involving 110 proteins and 86 outcomes.
